name: Adoram
bio:
Adoram was in charge of the forced labor in David's royal administration, listed among David's officials after Sheba's revolt was put down (2 Samuel 20:24). He continued in this same role — now called Adoniram, son of Abda — under Solomon's administration, overseeing the tribute of forced labor across Solomon's kingdom (1 Kings 4:6). When Solomon conscripted thirty thousand workers from across Israel to supply labor for the temple project, sending them to Lebanon in rotating shifts of ten thousand a month, it was Adoniram who was placed in charge of this labor force (1 Kings 5:13-14).

After Solomon's death, when Rehoboam's harsh response to the northern tribes' request for relief drove them to reject his rule, Rehoboam sent Adoram — the very man associated with the forced labor the people most resented — to try to assert his authority over them. All Israel stoned him to death on the spot, and Rehoboam himself had to flee by chariot to escape the same fate; Adoram's death marked the final, violent breaking point of the revolt that split Solomon's kingdom in two (1 Kings 12:18).
